translations.text: King Astyages was gathered to his ancestors, and Cyrus the Persian took over his kingdom.
Daniel was held in honor alongside the king. He lived with the king and was more highly honored than all the king’s friends.
The Babylonians had an idol named Bel. Every day they spent on him twelve artabas of fine flour, forty rams, and six metretes of wine.
The king himself revered him and went every day to worship him, but Daniel worshiped God. The king said to Daniel, “Why do you not worship Bel, my god?”

Daniel said to him, “I do not worship an image, an idol, or a carved figure, because it is the work of human hands. Instead, I revere the living God, who made heaven and earth and is Lord over all flesh. He is the one I worship.”
The king said to Daniel, “Does it not seem to you that Bel is alive? Or do you not see that he eats and drinks every day?”
Then Daniel laughed and said to the king, “Do not be mistaken, O king. This thing is clay on the inside and bronze on the outside. It has never eaten or drunk anything in its life.”
Then the king became angry, called Bel’s priests, and said to them, “Unless you tell me who eats all these provisions, you will die.
But if you show me that Bel is the one who eats them, Daniel will die, because he has blasphemed against Bel.” Daniel said to the king, “Let it be as you have said, O king.”
There were seventy priests of Bel, apart from their wives and children. The king went with Daniel to Bel’s temple.
The priests said to the king, “Look, we are going outside. But you, O king, set out the food for Bel, mix the wine and set it out, then close the door and seal it with your signet ring.
Come early in the morning. If you do not find that Bel has eaten all the food, let us die. But if Bel has eaten it, let Daniel die, because he has spoken blasphemously against us.”

They were confident because a secret entrance had been made for them beneath the table. Through it they used to come and go, eating everything that was set out for Bel and taking away whatever was left over.

When Bel’s priests had gone out, the king brought the food, filled the table, and set it before Bel. He also filled the vessels with wine, as was their custom, and went out. Daniel said to his servants, “Bring me ashes.” They brought him ashes, and he sifted them through a sieve throughout Bel’s temple in the king’s presence. The king watched and went out. He closed the door and sealed it with his own signet ring and Daniel’s signet ring.
The priests went in at night, as they were accustomed to do, with their wives and children. They ate everything that had been set out for Bel and drank the wine.
The king rose early in the morning, with Daniel beside him, and they went there.
The king said to Daniel, “Are the seals intact, Daniel?” Daniel said, “They are intact, my lord the king.”

When he opened the door, the king looked closely at the table and saw that everything that had been set out for Bel had been eaten. He cried out loudly from outside the doorway, “You are great, Bel, and there is not even the slightest deceit in you!”
Then Daniel laughed and held the king back from going inside for the moment. Daniel said to the king, “Look, my lord the king, and examine the floor. Whose footprints are these?”
The king said, “I see footprints of men, women, and children on the floor.”

Then the king became angry and arrested the priests, their wives, and their children. They showed the king the secret entrance they had, through which they used to come and go and eat everything that was set out on the table for Bel.
The king killed them all and gave Bel to Daniel as a gift. Daniel smashed him and demolished his temple.
There was also a great dragon there, which the Babylonians worshiped.
The king said to Daniel, “Now you cannot say that this one is not a god. Worship him, because he is a living god.”
Daniel said to the king, “I worship the Lord God, because he is the living God.”
“But you, O king, give me authority over it, and I will kill this dragon without a sword or a club.” The king said to him, “It is granted to you.”

Daniel took pitch, hair, and fat, boiled them together, made balls from them, and threw them into the dragon’s mouth. The dragon swallowed them, burst open, and died. Daniel said, “Look at what you worship, Babylonians!”

When the Babylonians heard, they were greatly distressed. They gathered against the king and turned against him, saying to one another, “The king has become a Jew! He has smashed Bel, killed the dragon, and killed the priests.”
They came to the king and said to him, “Either hand Daniel over to us, or we will kill you and your household.”
The king saw that they had all risen against him together. He was under pressure, and he was forced to hand Daniel over to them.
They took Daniel away and threw him into the lions’ den. He remained there for six days, so that the lions would grow hungry and eat him.
There were seven lions in that den. They used to give them two carcasses and two rams each day, but during those days they gave them nothing to eat, so that they would grow hungry and eat Daniel.
Now the prophet Habakkuk was in Judea. He had cooked a stew, broken bread into a bowl, and put the stew in it. He was going to take it to the reapers in the field.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Go, take this food you are carrying to Daniel, who has been thrown into the lions’ den in Babylon.”
Habakkuk said, “My lord, I have never seen Babylon, and I do not know the den.”
The angel placed his hand on Habakkuk’s head, lifted him by the hair of his head, and set him in Babylon above the den, by the power of the Holy Spirit.
Habakkuk called out and said, “Daniel, Daniel, get up and take this meal that God has sent you.”
Daniel said, “God has remembered me and has not withheld his mercy from me, for I know that you do not abandon those who love you.”
Daniel got up and ate. At that very moment, the angel took Habakkuk and set him in the place from which he had taken him before.
On the seventh day, the king came to mourn for Daniel, because he was grieved over him. He came to the den, peered into it, and saw Daniel sitting there.
He cried out loudly and said, “Great is the God of Daniel!”

He brought him up out of the den. Then he threw Daniel’s enemies, who had accused him and had sought to kill him, into the den. At that very moment, the lions ate them in front of the king and Daniel.
